title: Yoma Yangon International Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Yoma Yangon International Marathon Review: Course, Heat, Rules
meta_description: Yoma Yangon International Marathon review: the 2026 return after five years, a 5am half-marathon loop via the Strand and Shwedagon Pagoda Road, 25°C and 89% humidity, a 4-hour cut-off.
dek: What Myanmar's biggest running event was like when it came back in February 2026: the half-marathon loop through downtown Yangon, the humid pre-dawn air, the water and cut-off rules, and what an overseas runner needs to sort out first.
verdict: Enter if you want a well-attended half marathon through the centre of Yangon and can live with a few restrictions. The 2026 race, the first since January 2020, drew about 7,300 runners, some 240 of them from abroad, to a 21 km loop from Thuwunna down to the Strand and up Shwedagon Pagoda Road, with a four-hour limit that suits slower runners. The catch is the air and the rules. At the 5am start it was 25°C with 89% humidity, and runners may not carry any drinks, so you depend on about eight water points. Despite the name there is no full marathon. Get a visa before you fly, bring clean US dollars, and read the UK travel advice first.

sections.heading: The Course: One Loop Through Downtown Yangon
paragraphs: All three races started and finished at the National Indoor Stadium (1) in Thuwunna, on Waizayanta Road in Thingangyun Township [1][2]. The half marathon is one big loop. It heads south down Thanthumar and Upper Pazundaung roads, passes the 5 km mark at Set Yone Road, and follows Lower Pazundaung Road into the city centre, reaching Maha Bandula Road at about 7 km and Sandaku Road and the Strand at 8 km [3][4].

From there it runs west along the Strand for about three kilometres, then turns north up Shwedagon Pagoda Road from about 11 km to 13 km. It swings east along U Htaung Bo and Kan Yeik Tha roads at 14 and 15 km, and comes home up Banyardala, Kyaik Ka San and Pin Shwe Nyaung roads, passing 20 km on Lay Daung Kan Road before the finish on Waizayanta Road [3][4]. One British runner in their late sixties told Xinhua they especially enjoyed the stretch leading up to Shwedagon Pagoda [5].

The 10 km uses the first and last parts of the same loop, cutting across on Set Yone Road; the 5 km is an out-and-back on Thanthumar and Upper Pazundaung roads [4][3]. The map carries a note that routes are subject to adjustment, and no elevation profile was published [3].

The race used to be longer. Earlier editions included a full 42 km marathon, but the 2026 race offered only the half marathon, 10 km and 5 km [2]. The last edition before the break was run in January 2020 [6], and the organiser says that race had more than 10,000 runners [7].

sections.heading: The Weather: 25°C and Saturated Before Dawn
paragraphs: Yangon International Airport, about 11 km north-west of the stadium, recorded 25°C at 5am on race morning, with a dew point of 23°C, 89% humidity and a 5-knot wind [8]. The air did not change for three hours: it was still 25°C and 89% at 8am. Then it warmed, to 26°C at 8.30am and 27°C, with a dew point of 24°C and 84% humidity, at 9am, when the four-hour half-marathon limit ran out [8].

A dew point of 23°C to 24°C means sweat barely evaporates, so even the cool-looking 25°C start is hard work over 21 km. The 10 km and 5 km started later, at 6.30am and 7.30am [1], into the same saturated air, and the wind was only 2 knots from 6am onwards [8].

sections.heading: Water, Cut-offs and the No-Bottles Rule
paragraphs: The organiser banned every kind of liquid container at the event, including your own water bottle and energy drinks; hydration was to come only from the official water stations [1][9]. The half-marathon map marks eight hydration stations, roughly every 2 to 3 km, from Thanthumar Road to the last one near 19 km on Kyaik Ka San Road [3]. Volunteers and spectators also offered water along parts of the route [5].

The cut-offs are generous: four hours for the half marathon, two hours for the 10 km and an hour and a half for the 5 km. Runners outside the limit do not get the finisher medal [1]. Only the half marathon and 10 km were chip-timed, and only those runners get an e-certificate; the 5 km was not a timed race [9][1]. Runners who miss their category's flag-off are not allowed to start [9].
There was no bag storage. The organiser banned baggage and large items at the venue and told runners to arrive in running kit carrying only a phone and ID in a waist pouch [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The race is aimed at a broad field. Xinhua described runners from elite athletes to amateurs and youth teams [5]. Among the international runners it interviewed, one Irish runner finished the half marathon in 2 hours 30 minutes, and a 52-year-old from Singapore, running it for the first time, said it was very well organised [5].

There is money for a good club runner. The top ten men and women in both the half marathon and the 10 km won cash: in the half, K3,000,000 for first, K2,000,000 for second, K1,500,000 for third and K500,000 each for fourth to tenth; in the 10 km, K1,500,000 for first down to K200,000 each for fourth to tenth [4][1].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race packs, with the runner T-shirt, bib and race guide, were collected at the stadium from Thursday to Saturday, 19 to 21 February, 9am to 4pm, on showing the ID or passport used to register [1]. Overseas runners could also collect theirs on race morning, from 4am to 11.30am [10].

Fees depend on nationality. The half marathon cost 120,000 Ks for Myanmar nationals and 200,000 Ks for foreigners, with an early-bird rate of 102,000 Ks and 170,000 Ks until 7 December 2025; the 10 km was 75,000 Ks and 150,000 Ks [1]. Runners on the local rate without the right ID had to pay the difference or lose the place without a refund. International runners paid by Visa or JCB card [1]. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred, and you cannot change category [1]. Registration for the 2026 Yangon race had already closed by 9 December 2025 [11]. The minimum age for the half marathon was 16 [1].

All foreign visitors need a visa; the organiser points to the government e-visa site [10]. The UK government says you cannot get a visa on arrival and that Myanmar is largely a cash-based society [12]. The organiser advises bringing US dollars in good condition, because worn, creased or marked notes are generally refused [10].

Yangon Region is not on the list of areas the UK government advises against travelling to, but it describes the conflict in Myanmar as increasingly volatile and says the security situation may deteriorate at short notice [12]. Read the current advice before you book.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a half marathon through the centre of Yangon, from the riverside Strand to Shwedagon Pagoda Road, with a four-hour limit and a crowd that turns out to hand you water. The 5 km drew first-time racers and small children in 2026 [5].
Think twice if you want a full marathon or a fast time, or if you rely on carrying your own drinks: none of that was possible in 2026 [2][1].

The organiser's website says it is looking ahead to the 2027 edition but had published no date, fees or start times when this was written [13]. Check the travel advice and the visa rules before you commit.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information, rules and route map, airport weather records, English and Burmese news reports, runners interviewed by Xinhua, and UK government travel advice.

faqs.question: What time does the Yoma Yangon International Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Early. In 2026 the half marathon started at 5am, the 10 km at 6.30am and the 5 km at 7.30am, all from the National Indoor Stadium (1) in Thuwunna. Yangon's airport recorded 25°C and 89% humidity at the 5am start. Start times for the 2027 race had not been published yet.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off time for the Yoma Yangon half marathon?
faqs.answer: Four hours. In 2026 the half marathon had a four-hour limit, the 10 km two hours and the 5 km an hour and a half. Runners who finish outside the limit do not receive the finisher medal, and anyone who misses their category's flag-off is not allowed to start.

faqs.question: Can you carry your own water at the Yoma Yangon International Marathon?
faqs.answer: No. The 2026 rules banned every kind of liquid container, including personal water bottles and energy drinks, so runners relied on the official water stations. The half-marathon map marks eight hydration stations, roughly every 2 to 3 km, and volunteers also handed out water along parts of the route.

faqs.question: How much does the Yoma Yangon half marathon cost for foreigners?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the half marathon cost 200,000 Ks for foreigners, or 170,000 Ks at the early-bird rate before 7 December 2025, against 120,000 Ks for Myanmar nationals. International runners paid by Visa or JCB card. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred, and registration had closed by 9 December 2025.

faqs.question: What should overseas runners know before running in Yangon?
faqs.answer: Get a visa before you fly, because there is no visa on arrival, and bring clean US dollars, as Myanmar runs largely on cash. Overseas runners could collect race packs on race morning in 2026. Yangon is not on the UK's no-travel list, but read the current advice before booking.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the review template. Written about the previous edition (22 February 2026). Weather is from airport METAR observations, not a forecast. No public results page was found, so there are no winning times or finisher counts. No runner blogs or forum accounts were found; runner views come from Xinhua's interviews. The organiser's text says prize money goes to the first three, but its own prize table and the state-media report include fourth to tenth, so the table is used. The state-media route list names Shwedagon Pagoda as a road; the map labels it Shwedagon Pagoda Road. Field figures differ slightly (more than 7,000 in state media, about 7,300 from the organiser via Xinhua); the review uses the organiser figure. The Xinhua Myanmar Burmese report returned 410 Gone; GNLM and Ahotu returned 403. No 2027 date was found. No rating.
